summary: Deer Harbor SPB (DHB) is a small public-use seaplane base located on Orcas Island in Washington State's San Juan Islands archipelago. Situated on the protected waters of Deer Harbor, it primarily serves general aviation floatplanes connecting the islands to the mainland. The base provides a scenic gateway to one of the Pacific Northwest's most popular island destinations, known for whale watching, kayaking, and charming rural communities.
faqs:
Q: What type of aircraft use Deer Harbor SPB?
A: It primarily serves single-engine floatplanes operated by charter services, as it is a seaplane base without paved runways.

Q: Where is Deer Harbor SPB located?
A: It is situated on the northeastern side of Orcas Island in the San Juan Islands of Washington State, within the sheltered waters of Deer Harbor.

Q: Are there scheduled airline services at this airport?
A: No regular scheduled commercial flights operate here; the facility mainly handles charter and private floatplane operations.

Q: Can visitors rent cars or arrange ground transport at the seaplane base?
A: Limited ground transportation is available, typically requiring advance arrangements with local taxi services or shuttle providers on Orcas Island.
transport_tips: Since this is a seaplane base accessed only by water or by road from other parts of Orcas Island, visitors typically arrive via private or chartered floatplane. Getting to the dock area from other parts of the island requires a rental car, taxi, or pre-arranged shuttle, as public transit options are very limited. The nearest ferry terminal is at Orcas Village, approximately a 15-minute drive from Deer Harbor.
local_tip: Visit during the summer months and time your seaplane landing for late afternoon—the golden light over the San Juan Islands makes for stunning aerial views, and the calm evening winds typically provide smoother landings on the harbor.
